idiom_name: blocks, procs and Rack's call(env) object protocol (ActiveSupport::Callbacks)
implementation_notes: Ruby expresses inversion with blocks, procs and a message the framework sends: a Rack application is any object that responds to call(env), and the server calls it once per request, while ActiveSupport::Callbacks lets a class declare before/around/after hooks that run_callbacks invokes around its own event. The classic framework base class is replaced by an object protocol or block registration, which is why Rack middleware and Rails filters are ordinary objects and procs. Declaring an abstract base class is still justified when the host must document several related extension points, but the protocolar form is the idiomatic default.
code_sketch:
# Rack: the server owns the loop and calls your object per request.
class Orders
  def call(env)                          # called by the Rack server
    [200, { "content-type" => "text/plain" }, ["orders"]]
  end
end
run Orders.new                           # config.ru registration

class Account
  include ActiveSupport::Callbacks
  set_callback :save, :before, :audit    # the framework runs it around save
end
pitfalls: A Rack server may call the app object concurrently, so instance variables shared across requests are unsafe unless frozen or synchronised.
Blocks passed to a framework are often evaluated in the framework's context (instance_exec), so self and method lookup inside a callback can differ from the enclosing class.
